title: Anthropic might be developing its own voice models
key_facts: TestingCatalog spotted a separate hidden 'Voice' item in Claude's web navigation labeled 'Preview', which refers to Anthropic's internal preview environment, not a public release.
No details have surfaced on what the interface would offer or how it differs from Claude's existing voice mode.
Anthropic recently added an optional, off-by-default setting letting users share voice recordings and conversation data for model training, separate from the consent for text conversations.
TestingCatalog says collecting this data could indicate Anthropic is preparing its own speech models, but it could also support existing voice features.
Claude already supports voice conversations on mobile, desktop and web, using its language models to process speech and generate spoken replies.

Anthropic previously held talks with ElevenLabs about voice partnerships; the underlying voice provider has not been officially confirmed, and Anthropic has not released its own text-to-speech models through its API.
quote_evidence: No details have surfaced about what the interface would offer or how it might differ from Claude’s existing voice mode.
However, it remains unclear whether Anthropic is developing a real-time voice model, redesigning the interface, or testing something entirely different.
There is also no indication of when this experiment could become publicly available.
why_it_matters_hint: A hidden menu item and a new data-sharing setting hint at Anthropic work on voice, but nothing is confirmed.
notes: Read TestingCatalog in full. Single-outlet sighting of an unreleased feature; the voice-data setting is circumstantial and TestingCatalog itself says it could support existing voice features.
